lesson.title: A Day in Paris: Reading
lesson.subtitle: The capstone narrative in Paris synthesizing all 9 conversion bridges and tense frames.

hook.title: A Day in Paris: Reading & Building Connected Narrative
hook.content: Follow a full day in Paris from morning arrival at la gare (Je suis arrivé à la gare) to walking through the city (la ville était belle) and meeting a friend who lives there (qui habite ici depuis cinq ans).

footnotes.title: Notice how every clause links with que, qui, où, or parce que
footnotes.content: Connected French is simple clauses welded together with quand, parce que, qui, que, and où.

pattern.title: Scene (Imparfait) + Action (Passé Composé) + Ongoing Truth (Present + depuis)
pattern.content: Read and assemble connected multi-clause sentences set in Paris.
pattern.linguist_note: Narrative cohesion in French relies on tense-aspect switching and relative subordination.
pattern.trap_note: Keep each clause's tense true to its job: ongoing residence = Present + depuis; background scene = Imparfait; completed steps = Passé composé!

exercises.prompt: Match each clause from the Paris story with its tense and job:

matching_pairs.english: Je suis arrivé à la gare ce matin
J'ai vu mon ami qui habite à Paris depuis trois ans
On va dîner au restaurant ce soir

exercises.target_answer: Passé composé (être): completed arrival, Imparfait: background description, Passé composé + Present with depuis, Near future: evening plan
exercises.meaning: Je suis arrivé à la gare ce matin, La ville était très belle, J'ai vu mon ami qui habite à Paris depuis trois ans, On va dîner au restaurant ce soir
exercises.explanation: Four tenses cooperate seamlessly inside one story.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentences capture the meaning of 'Je suis allé au café où mon ami m'attendait'?
exercises.german: Je suis allé au café où mon ami m'attendait
exercises.meaning: I went to the café where my friend was waiting for me
renderings: I went to the café where my friend was waiting for me
I walked to the café where my friend was waiting
traps: I am going to the café where my friend waits
My friend went to the café where I was waiting
exercises.target_answer: I went to the café where my friend was waiting for me
exercises.explanation: Je suis allé is the completed motion; m'attendait (-ait) is the ongoing background action.

exercises.prompt: What is the literal structure of 'L'ami que j'ai vu habite ici depuis deux ans'?
exercises.german: L'ami que j'ai vu habite ici depuis deux ans
exercises.natural: The friend whom I saw has lived here for two years
options: The friend whom I saw has lived here for two years
The friend who saw me lived here two years ago
The-friend that I have seen lives here since two years
exercises.target_answer: The-friend that I have seen lives here since two years
exercises.meaning: Literal structure: The-friend that I have seen lives here since two years
exercises.explanation: que j'ai vu modifies L'ami, and habite ici depuis deux ans uses the present tense.

exercises.idea: I arrived in Paris this morning and the city is very beautiful
cues: I arrived in Paris this morning → Je suis arrivé à Paris ce matin
and the city is very beautiful → et la ville est très belle
idea_parts: past arrival → Je suis arrivé à Paris ce matin
description → et la ville est très belle
exercises.target_answer: Je suis arrivé à Paris ce matin et la ville est très belle
exercises.meaning: I arrived in Paris this morning and the city is very beautiful
exercises.explanation: arriver takes être (Je suis arrivé) and cities take à (à Paris).

diagnosis.cue: arriver takes être: Je suis arrivé.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Nous avons trouvé un petit bistro près de la gare
exercises.target_answer: Nous avons trouvé un petit bistro près de la gare
exercises.meaning: We found a small bistro near the station
cues: un petit bistro près de la gare
exercises.explanation: trouvé (-é) with avons + BAGS adjective petit before bistro.
exercises.affirmation: You wrote the Paris narrative sentence cleanly.

summary.outcome: Read and construct multi-clause French narratives combining past events, background descriptions, and ongoing states.

use_example.german: Quand je suis sorti de la gare, j'ai vu que la ville était magnifique.
use_example.english: When I walked out of the station, I saw that the city was magnificent.

summary.takeaway: Real stories weave Passé composé (events), Imparfait (scene), and Present + depuis (ongoing truths).
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([3002] Trap Watch: False Friends in the Wild): see how A Day in Paris: Reading leads directly into Trap Watch: False Friends in the Wild.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "I arrived in Paris this morning and the city is very beautiful" in French:
twist.target_answer: Je suis arrivé à Paris ce matin et la ville est très belle
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Je suis arrivé à Paris ce matin et la ville est très belle" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of A Day in Paris: Reading.

ville.etymology_derivation: Latin vīlla 'country estate' grew into the whole city in French (leaving 'city' as la cité for the historic core).

hôtel.shift_rule: Norman doublet: S and H dropped
hôtel.etymology_derivation: Latin hospitalis → hostel AND hôtel — the same word entered English twice: once with its S (hostel, hospital), once without (hôtel).

gare.etymology_derivation: Originally a river shelter where boats pulled in.

train.context_phrase: Le train part à huit heures.
train.etymology_derivation: Old French traïn 'a line of things pulled along'.

restaurant.etymology_derivation: From restaurer 'to restore' — originally a restoring broth sold in Paris in 1765.

café.etymology_derivation: Turkish kahve → Italian caffè → French café. English took the same journey twice: coffee and café.

ami.etymology_derivation: In liaison, un ami sounds like /œ̃.na.mi/ and mes amis like /me.za.mi/.

depuis.context_translation: I have lived here for three years (lit. I live here since three years).
depuis.etymology_derivation: Because the action is still true right now, French uses the PRESENT tense with depuis!

était.etymology_derivation: être's imparfait — the background tense, the was of a story already in motion.

arrivé.etymology_derivation: Late Latin ad rīpam 'to the shore' — to arrive was to land on a riverbank.
